The next major update to Teslascope is now under active development and will launch this Summer! There's no slowing us down.

In addition, we will publicly open our iOS TestFlight app later this week following Apple's approval of an update.

This Summer will be hot! ☀️

The next major update focuses heavily on refinements to existing features, such as drives, charging, and software.

New data visualizations, real-time dashboards, better controls for sharing.

Groups are receiving substantial upgrades w/ new event planning and easier management.

Our subscribers here on X will get sneak peeks at many of these upcoming features.

We continually strive to build software and experiences that positively benefit the global Tesla community, whether a guest, member, or subscriber.

We look forward to sharing more details soon.

ICYMI: The viral (and unfortunately fatal) crash in Texas was due to the driver pressing down on the accelerator and reaching a top speed of 73 mph.

Reckless driving costs lives and the media’s desire to find AP / Full Self-Driving at fault makes roads less safe for everyone.


Ashok Elluswamy (@aelluswamy)

Yup. In this case, the driver manually overrode self-driving by pressing the accelerator all the way to 100% of the accel pedal in this residential area. They reached a speed of 73 mph during the crash, and had the accelerator pressed even after the crash.
